## p169 A — Repeated station-control report

**Edition context:** Station control and the Seifert service exchange.

**Related source pages:** [p168 A](168.md#source-p168-a), [p168 B](168.md#source-p168-b), [p172 A](172.md#source-p172-a), [p172 B](172.md#source-p172-b), [p174 B](174.md#source-p174-b), [p174 C](174.md#source-p174-c), [p174 D](174.md#source-p174-d), [p174 E](174.md#source-p174-e).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-station-control-and-the-seifert-service-exchange"></a>


[Source certificate](../../experiments/p170_continuation/seifert_records.json)

**Nine source records, seven message groups.** The 7–9 November and 10–12 November published keys recover a sequence of radio-station reports and short service messages. Two pairs are repeated transmissions. These records are outside the original 22-entry challenge; the open p170 challenge is section **A**, not any of these neighboring records.

Source transcription, cipher checks and editorial work: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The station-control interpretations of p168 A and B were already published by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**; their author manuscript discusses both on printed p23 / PDF page 24. The keys retain their recorded historical and modern provenance. This page provides a source-level edition, without claiming a first historical decipherment.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-conditional-shared-digits"></a>

### Conditional shared digits

The paired monitoring orders each gain their hundreds digit: **500**. Both physical receptions have the same complete ciphertext; repetition preserves the value once the shared square is interpreted. No source coordinate is changed. The [joint reconstruction](../../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> Sofort US 500 hoeren.

<summary>Exact conditional labels</summary>

**Edited output — p172_B, conditional shared square; 20/20 fixed positions:**

```text
SOFORTXUSX500XHOEREN
```

**Edited output — p174_D, conditional shared square; 20/20 fixed positions:**

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-read-the-messages"></a>

### Read the messages

The prior body credit for p168 A also applies to its repeated content at
**p169 A**. Identification of the repeat, its exact coordinate differences,
and the present source edition remain our contribution.

Square brackets mark supplied letters or abbreviation expansions. Punctuation, capitalization and word spacing are editorial.

| Source | Readable German | Meaning and exact qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **p168 A**; repeated with errors at **p169 A** | Stehe ab 2200 unter Aufsicht Sol[d]atenrats. Stat[ion und] Personal fest in meiner Hand. Betrieb unverändert. Seifert. | From 22:00 the sender is under the soldiers' council's supervision; station/personnel remain firmly under his control and operation is unchanged. All 92 raw positions of p168 A decode exactly; the source spells `SOLATENRATS` without `D`. The connecting words in the `STATPERSONAL` expansion are editorial. |
| **p168 B** | Soldatenrat Cöln wird bald Funkstelle besetzen. Versucht schon Funksprüche aufzugeben. | Cologne's soldiers' council is expected to occupy the radio station and is already trying to submit radio messages. The raw text has `SOLDATENRA9` and `SCKON`; the readable version requires two explicit coordinate substitutions. |
| **p172 A** | Akten [s]ämtlich vernichtet. Schlüssel in pers[önlicher] Obhut noch vorhanden. Seifert. | All records have been destroyed; the cipher keys remain in personal custody. The source fixes 67/68 plaintext positions. One invalid printed glyph leaves the initial letter of `SAEMTLICH` unresolved; `S` is a supported reading, not a source-observed letter. |
| **p174 B** | Wenn Seifert eingetroffe[n], bitte Nachr[icht]. TOF. | Please report when Seifert has arrived. The source fixes 36/37 positions. One doubtful glyph permits `N`; a `G` interpretation of that glyph instead produces separator `X` after the raw spelling `EINGETROFFE`. `TOF` is not expanded. |
| **p174 C** | Wann Rückkunft Seifert? RE. | When will Seifert return? All 24 plaintext positions decode exactly. `RE` remains unexpanded. |
| **p172 B / p174 D** | Sofort US ?00 hören. | An immediate listening instruction. The two 40-coordinate copies are identical. The unknown hundreds digit can be **5, 6, 7, 8 or 9** under a globally consistent completion of the published square. The role of `US` and the units of the number are not established. |
| **p174 E** | Seifert abgefahren. RENTE. | Seifert has departed. The raw text is `SQIFQRTABGEFAHRENXRENTE`; restoring the name requires two explicit `G → X` coordinate substitutions. `RENTE` is retained literally. |

The shared surname connects the service records, but the surviving headers do not establish Seifert's full name or a complete itinerary. The printed time expressions are preserved in the certificate, including the anomalous `17.28 p.m.` in p174 E. The day digit in p172 B is overtyped; the identical p174 D copy is explicitly dated 12 November.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-p168-b--160-coordinates--80-positions"></a>

#### p168 B — 160 coordinates / 80 positions

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
SOLDATENRA9XCOELNXWIRDBALDFUNKSTELLEBESETZENXVERSUCHTSCKONFUNKSPRUECHEAUFZUGEBEN
```

</details>

At zero-based ciphertext positions **89** and **141**, `F → V` and `G → X` give `SOLDATENRAT` and `SCHON`. The other **158 coordinates remain unchanged**. These are proposed source emendations, not alternative square assignments.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-p172-a--136-slots--68-positions"></a>

#### p172 A — 136 slots / 68 positions

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
AKTEN?AEMTLICHVERNICHTETXSCHLUESSELINPERSOBHUTNOCHVORHANDENXXSEIFERT
```

</details>

The [source](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p172_AB.png) prints `DAAGC`: its final `C` is outside the ADFGVX alphabet and becomes one erasure at ciphertext position **119**. The plaintext domain at position **5** is exactly `{F,I,K,N,O,S}`. Filling that coordinate with `G` gives `S` and preserves all **135 valid received coordinates**. `PERSOBHUT` is retained; the readable expansion is *pers[önlicher] Obhut*.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-p174-b--74-slots--37-positions"></a>

#### p174 B — 74 slots / 37 positions

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WENNSEIFERTEINGETROFFE?BITTENACHRXTOF
```

</details>

The [source excerpt](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p174_BCDE.png) shows a `C`-like or defective `G` glyph at the start of group `CVXXF`, ciphertext position **20**. Its conservative analysis is `?VXXF`. The uncertain plaintext position **22** has domain `{1,5,6,7,8,9,E,N,V,X}`.

The readable `N` completion uses **D** at the source erasure and preserves all **73 certain coordinates**. Reading the doubtful glyph as **G** instead gives:

**Conditional interpretation — alternate G reading of the doubtful source glyph:**

```text
WENNSEIFERTEINGETROFFEXBITTENACHRXTOF
```

Within that single-source analysis, both alternatives are retained; the complete word `EINGETROFFEN` is an editorial inference.

An independent [p183 B witness](183.md#edition-cases-radio-nov12-arrival-departure-and-car-p183-b)
now supplies observed `D` at source index 20 and therefore `N` at plaintext
position 22. Together the two conservative source transcriptions support
every target pair. The original C/G-like appearance and its G-reading
alternative remain in the earlier certificate and source analysis above.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-the-p169-a-repeat"></a>

### The p169 A repeat

[p169 A](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p169_A.png) carries the same `SY v GK`, `2000` and `RICHI-184` metadata as p168 A, with a later intercept time. It prints **185 coordinates**, including the six-character group `DGDGGX`.

Deleting either adjacent `G` at zero-based source position **158** or **159** gives the same 184-coordinate conditional layer and this raw decipherment:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional deletion of source 158 or 159; equivalent aliases retained:**

```text
STEHEAB2200UNTEYAUFSICHTSOLATENRATWXSTATPERSONALFESTINMEIKERHANDXBETRIEBUNVERAENDURTXSEIFERT
```

</details>

It supports the repeated-message identification but is less clean than p168 A. Both deletion aliases are recorded. The untouched odd-length source is retained and is never silently decoded after dropping its last coordinate.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-evidence-and-reproduction"></a>

### Evidence and reproduction

The [certificate](../../experiments/p170_continuation/seifert_records.json) contains all nine literal source transcriptions, original headers, partial keys, raw plaintext domains, cropped-image hashes and exact proposed edits. It applies the already published keys; no unknown square cell is fixed by the prose.

```sh
python experiments/p170_continuation/verify_seifert.py
python experiments/p170_continuation/verify_seifert.py --json
```

The independent verifier checks **913 source slots**, every source-preserving fill, the four explicit coordinate substitutions, the p169 deletion aliases, both identical service copies, and all five globally attainable digit readings. A local copy of the source PDF can additionally be bound by SHA-256 with `--pdf /path/to/childs.pdf`.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-sources-and-priority"></a>

#### Sources and priority

- **J. Rives Childs collection:** printed pp168, 169, 172 and 174; PDF page 171, 172, 175 and 177 in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view). The certificate retains its hash and the exact section headers.
- **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker:** *Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of World War I*, [author manuscript](https://www.apprendre-en-ligne.net/crypto/bibliotheque/PDF/adfgvx.pdf), printed p23 / PDF page 24. This earlier work explicitly identifies the p168 A/B station-control reports; it also credits Childs's wartime decipherment of the Cologne message. The present edition does not reassign that priority.
- **Published keys:** [key catalog](../../data/keys.json), entries `Nov7-9` and `Nov10-12`, retaining original table and solver provenance.

## p169 B — Forward station and construction trains to Group Winterfeld

**Edition context:** Gomel route derailment and station-train forwarding.

**Related source pages:** [p155 D](155.md#source-p155-d).

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-derailment-and-trains-gomel-route-derailment-and-station-train-forwarding"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Two source editions concern railway operations: a freight-train derailment blocking both tracks on the proposed Gomel–Bachmatsch route, and a message about forwarding a station train and construction train to Group Winterfeld. The wagon count, train labels, abbreviations and office references remain literal.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-derailment-and-trains-p169-b-1"></a>

### p169 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) ZM v SY (10.00 p.m., November 9th); 2245 (9/11); RICHI-224`

**Readable German:** based on the unchanged raw output.

> NACHRUEBGEL. FECH wird beschleunigt Stationszug S11?2 und Bauzug 1924 der Gruppe Winterfeld zufuehren. Nachchef 1B1??1?.

**Meaning:** The station train labelled S11?2 and construction train labelled 1924 are to be forwarded promptly to Group Winterfeld. The opening NACHRUEBGEL and FECH are preserved without forcing an expansion, and the train and office labels are not independently numbered.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
NACHRUEBGELXFECHWIRDBESCHLEUNIGTSTATIONSZUGXS11?2XUNDBAUZUGX1924XDERGRUPPEXWINTERFELDZUFUEHRENXNACHCHEFX1B1??1?X
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The complete 224-slot source frame requires no observed-coordinate substitution or source-mask fill.
- DXGVV is a five-coordinate printed group; the older OCR included an extra uncertainty mark.
- The reference 1B1??1? and the station-train field retain all coupled unassigned square cells. A global witness is provided without claiming literal historical digit values.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-derailment-and-trains-conditional-shared-digits"></a>

The [Siegfried reference comparison](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) supplies one shared conditional assignment, XA=5 and VF=6, to both railway records.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-derailment-and-trains-p155-d"></a>

#### p155 D

**Readable German — conditional shared digits, with the existing source edition retained:**

> OK Mackensen. Morgenmeldung vom 7.11.18: Auf Strecke Gomel, Bachmatsch entgleiste ein Gueterzug. 25 Wagen zertruemmert. Beide Gleise sind gesperrt. Hrgr. Kiew. RM 1 A 7097 18.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-derailment-and-trains-coupled-wagon-and-train-labels"></a>

### Coupled wagon and train labels

The unresolved symbols are linked by the unchanged Nov7–9 square. All indices below are zero-based plaintext positions.

| Square cell | Source occurrences | Shared constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| XA | p155 D position 89; p169 B position 47 | The unknown in wagon label `2?` is the same label as the unknown in train label `S11?2`. |
| VF | p169 B positions 107, 108 and 110 | All three unknowns in `1B1??1?` are the same label, and differ from XA. |

VF and XA carry the two remaining labels `{5, 6}` bijectively. There are therefore two global assignments, not five independent numerical guesses. Neither assignment is established as the historical numbering.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-derailment-and-trains-evidence-and-credit"></a>

### Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For a partial output, an injective global completion of the square and residual source masks supplies an explicitly nonhistorical round-trip witness. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/nov7_derailment_and_trains/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A round-trip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-derailment-and-trains-p155-d-1"></a>

### p155 D

**Source transcription — header:** `D) NKJ v LP (3.55 p.m., November 7th); FUER UKS 1355; RICHI-316`

**Readable German:** based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> OK Mackensen. Morgenmeldung vom 7X11X18: Auf Strecke Gomel, Bachmatsch entgleiste ein Gueterzug. 2? Wagen zertruemmert. Beide Gleise sind gesperrt. Hrgr. Kiew RMX1XAX7097X18.

**Meaning:** A morning report addressed to Oberkommando Mackensen says a freight train derailed on the proposed Gomel–Bachmatsch route, that a quantity written 2? of wagons was wrecked, and that both tracks are blocked. The unresolved wagon-count label and final reference remain literal.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
OKXMACKENSENXXMORGENMELDUNGVOM7X11X18AUFSTRECKEXGOMELXBNCHMABSCH?ENBGLEISTEEI?GUETERZUG?2?WAGENZE?TRUEMMERT?BEIDEGLEISESINDGESPERRTXXHRGRXKIEWXRMX1XAX7097X18X
```

**Edited output** — 3 observed-coordinate substitutions and 5 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
OKXMACKENSENXXMORGENMELDUNGVOM7X11X18AUFSTRECKEXGOMELXBACHMATSCHXENTGLEISTEEINGUETERZUGX2?WAGENZERTRUEMMERTXBEIDEGLEISESINDGESPERRTXXHRGRXKIEWXRMX1XAX7097X18X
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The source has four dashes and a literal Y-shaped noncoordinate glyph in DXYVF. These five slots are masked before decoding and filled separately in the proposed reading.
- The place repair BNCHMABSCH to BACHMATSCH requires two observed-coordinate substitutions; the other substitution changes ENBGLEISTE to ENTGLEISTE. This is an explicit word proposal, not a new external geographical identification.
- The unknown in 2? is the globally unresolved XA cell, whose domain is {5,6} in the published Nov7–9 square. This edition does not choose 25 or 26 wagons.
- Correct source groups FVXDD and VXDVG each have five slots. Earlier OCR strings with repeated X coordinates are not treated as source evidence.

</details>
